2027-05-07.title: Friday of the Sixth Week of Easter
readings: Do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent; for I am with you
God is king of all the earth (or: Alleluia)
No one will take your joy from you
2027-05-07.alt: Easter weekday. The paschal candle burns beside the ambo; the Alleluia is sung before the Gospel; the Regina Caeli (Queen of Heaven) replaces the Angelus until Pentecost. Liturgical colour: white. First Friday of the month: in many parishes the Holy Hour, confessions and the devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus. From today until the Saturday before Pentecost, nine days in all, the Church may pray the novena to the Holy Spirit, as the apostles prayed with Mary in the upper room.
2027-05-07.verse: So you have pain now; but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
theo: Paul has been in Corinth for some time. He has been opposed, he has moved next door to the synagogue, and he has seen the synagogue official believe. Yet he is afraid. Writing to the Corinthians later, he admits it: “And I came to you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling” (1 Corinthians 2:3). He knew what usually came next in a city: riots, beatings, flight by night. So the Lord speaks to him in a vision: “Do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent; for I am with you, and no one will lay a hand on you to harm you, for there are many in this city who are my people.” The Lord does not promise that there will be no trouble. He promises his presence, and he gives Paul a new way of looking at the noisy port city: many in this city are already mine, though they do not know it yet. So Paul stays “a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them,” the longest stay of his journeys so far.

Then the trouble comes. When Gallio becomes proconsul of Achaia, some leaders of the Jewish community bring Paul before the tribunal, accusing him of persuading people to worship God against the law. Gallio, the brother of the philosopher Seneca, will not even hear Paul's defence: this is “a matter of questions about words and names and your own law, see to it yourselves.” An inscription found at Delphi dates Gallio's year in Corinth to about 51 or 52, and so this scene is one of the fixed points by which we date Paul's life. A Roman judge's indifference becomes, for a time, the protection of the Gospel. Paul stays on, then sails for Syria with Priscilla and Aquila, cutting his hair at Cenchreae because of a vow, a sign that he still lived as a devout Jew. Luke's phrase “the Jews” here means the group in that synagogue who opposed Paul, not the Jewish people; the official Crispus had believed, and Sosthenes, perhaps the same “brother Sosthenes” who later writes with Paul (1 Corinthians 1:1), suffers in the uproar.

The Gospel gives the image of a woman in labour: “she has pain, because her hour has come. But when her child is born, she no longer remembers the anguish because of the joy of having brought a human being into the world.” Jesus uses the word “hour,” the word he uses for his own Passion. His cross is a birth. On this First Friday the Church looks at the pierced Heart of Jesus. From his opened side came blood and water (John 19:34), and the Fathers saw there the birth of the Church, as Eve was formed from the side of the sleeping Adam. The pain of Good Friday was a labour, and its child is a new people. That is why the joy Jesus promises is a joy that “no one will take from you”: it is not a mood that comes and goes, but the life of the Risen One born in us. And the Psalm, an ancient song for the Lord's enthronement, already rings with Ascension joy: “Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout to God with loud songs of joy.”
conn: Like Jacob at Bethel (Genesis 28:15) and Jeremiah at his call (Jeremiah 1:8), Paul hears “I am with you.” Luke tells of several visions given to Paul at turning points (Acts 16:9; 23:11; 27:23–24).
“Many in this city are my people.”
Corinth was famous for its wealth and its loose living. The Lord sees not a hopeless city but a people still to be gathered.
Lucius Junius Gallio Annaeanus, brother of Seneca. An inscription at Delphi, a letter of the emperor Claudius, places his proconsulship in about AD 51–52.
The Greek bēma, a raised speaking platform. Its remains can still be seen in the forum of ancient Corinth.
Successor of Crispus as official of the synagogue. A Sosthenes is named with Paul at the start of 1 Corinthians; many think he is the same man, later a believer.
Probably a vow like the Nazirite vow (Numbers 6), ended by cutting the hair. Cenchreae, Corinth's eastern port, later had a church with “our sister Phoebe” as its deacon (Romans 16:1).
A psalm of God's kingship. Christian liturgy has long sung it on the Ascension: “God has gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet” (Psalm 47:5).
A prophetic image of the birth of the messianic age (Isaiah 26:17; 66:7–9). In John, Jesus' “hour” is the hour of his Passion and glorification (John 12:23; 13:1).

St Margaret Mary Alacoque (1647–1690) reported that the Lord asked for Communion of reparation on the first Friday of nine consecutive months. The devotion spread throughout the Church, and in India and Kerala it remains strong.
altar: The Heart of Jesus, opened on the cross, is not only a memory. At every Mass the same sacrifice is made present on the altar, and the Lord who was pierced gives us his Body and Blood, the fruit of his labour of love.
First Friday Communion is a way of answering love with love. We receive the Heart that was pierced for us and offer our own hearts, with their sins and sorrows, to be healed and set on fire.
outline: Ask a mother in the congregation, in your mind: do you remember the pain, or the face of your child?
Point 1 · Do not be afraid, but speak
The Lord's word to a fearful apostle.
Point 2 · Words and names and your own law
A judge who would not judge, and a door kept open.
The labour of the cross and the birth of joy.
A newborn laid on its mother's breast, and above, a crucifix with the side opened.
“No one will take your joy from you.”
live: Is there a truth of faith you have kept silent about at home or at work out of fear? Say it gently today.
Go to confession or spend a quiet half hour before the Blessed Sacrament this weekend, and consecrate your family to the Sacred Heart.
Pray each day until Pentecost: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love.
fathers: The Lord did not take away the danger from Paul; he took away the fear. He did not say: no one will attack you, but: no one will harm you, for I am with you. That is the courage of the saints.

From his side came water and blood, the signs of Baptism and the Eucharist. From these the Church is born. As God formed Eve from the side of Adam while he slept, so Christ gave us the Church from his side as he slept on the cross.
The joy that no one takes away is Christ himself. Every other joy can be lost; this one is kept in heaven, where he is, and so it is safe.
magis: Jesus knew and loved us each and all during his life, his agony and his Passion; his Sacred Heart, pierced by our sins and for our salvation, is the chief sign of that love.
The devotion to the Sacred Heart is the worship of the love of God for us shown in the Heart of Jesus.
“He loved us”: the Heart of Christ is the centre where we learn to love and are healed of an empty, heartless life.
The duty of Christians to take part in the life of the Church impels them to act as witnesses of the Gospel by word and deed.
The human person has a right to religious freedom; no one may be forced to act against conscience in religious matters.
saints: An Italian woman of Viterbo (1656–1728) who opened some of the first public schools for girls in Italy and founded the Venerini Sisters. She died on 7 May 1728 and was canonized in 2006.
9 May: THE ASCENSION OF THE LORD (in India); World Communications Day. 10 May: St John of Avila (optional). 11 May: Easter weekday.
2027-05-07.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you said to Paul in the night: do not be afraid, but speak, for I am with you. Speak that word to us. When we are silent from fear, give us courage; when we are opposed, give us patience; when we are protected, give us thanks. On this First Friday we come to your pierced Heart. From your opened side the Church was born; from your labour of love comes our joy. Take our hearts, heal them, and make them like yours. Send us your Holy Spirit, for whom we begin to wait with Mary your Mother, and give us the joy that no one can take from us. You live and reign for ever and ever. Alleluia. Amen.

quick: In a night vision the Lord told Paul: do not be afraid, speak, for I am with you; Paul stayed eighteen months in Corinth.
Gallio refused to judge a dispute about the Jewish law, and Paul was able to continue his work.
Jesus: like a woman in labour you have pain now, but I will see you again, and no one will take your joy from you.
2027-05-07.action: Pray an act of consecration to the Sacred Heart with your family tonight, and begin the novena to the Holy Spirit.
2027-05-07.question: Where am I silent out of fear when the Lord is asking me to speak?
catechism: Called to witness by word and deed.
kidsaint: Margaret Mary was a French sister who loved to pray before Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. Jesus showed her his Heart, burning with love for all people, and asked people to receive him in Holy Communion on the first Friday of the month. Lesson: Jesus' Heart is full of love for you; you can give him your heart too.
2027-05-07.special: Easter weekday; First Friday (Sacred Heart devotion). The novena to the Holy Spirit may begin today. Regina Caeli at noon.
term: The custom of going to confession and receiving Holy Communion on the first Friday of the month, in honour of the Sacred Heart of Jesus and in reparation for sins. It goes back to the revelations to St Margaret Mary in the seventeenth century.

family.explain: Jesus said that his friends would be sad for a while, like a mother when her baby is being born. But when the baby comes, the mother is so happy that she forgets the pain. Jesus' cross was painful, but from it came new life for us. Today is First Friday: we remember how much Jesus' Heart loves us.
family.intention: We pray for mothers who are expecting a baby, for babies being born today, and for all who are afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family needs courage today?” Place your hands on that person's shoulder and pray: Jesus, be with them; do not be afraid.

illus: A senior nurse who worked for thirty years in the labour room of a mission hospital in Thrissur used to say the same thing to every frightened young mother: in one hour you will forget all this, I promise you. The mothers never believed her during the pain, and always laughed about it afterwards with the baby in their arms. On the first Friday of every month she went to the hospital chapel before her shift. When a young doctor asked her why, she said: there I look at a Heart that went through labour for all of us. It helps me to tell the mothers the truth.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your Heart was pierced for us. Take away our fear and give us the joy that no one can take from us. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent (Acts 18:9). What am I afraid to say for Jesus?
There are many in this city who are my people (Acts 18:10). How do I look at my town or city: as hopeless, or as a place where God has his people?
No one will take your joy from you (John 16:22). What kind of joy do I live on: the kind that goes, or the kind that stays?
pm.resp: God is king of all the earth.
interc: For Christians who are afraid to speak of their faith, that the Lord may stand by them.
For judges and magistrates, that they may protect religious freedom and the rights of all.
For expectant mothers and for children about to be born.
For all who are devoted to the Sacred Heart, that they may grow in love and reparation.
For our group, beginning the novena to the Holy Spirit with Mary.
pm.close: Father, from the pierced Heart of your Son you gave birth to your Church. Fill us with the joy of the Resurrection, which no one can take from us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, we think of St Paul as a man without fear. Today's reading tells us otherwise. One night in Corinth the Lord speaks to him in a vision: do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent; for I am with you (Acts 18:9–10). The Lord would not say do not be afraid to someone who was not afraid.

Paul himself told the Corinthians later: I came to you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling. He had been beaten in other cities, chased out at night. Now in Corinth he wondered: will it happen again? And the Lord says: I am with you, and there are many in this city who are my people.

Notice what the Lord promises and what he does not. He does not promise that nobody will make trouble. Trouble does come: Paul is dragged before the judge Gallio. But the Lord keeps his word: no one harms him. The judge refuses the case, and Paul goes on preaching. God's protection sometimes comes through strange doors, even through the indifference of a Roman official.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of a mother in labour. She has pain because her hour has come, but when the child is born she forgets the pain because of her joy. Mothers here know this better than any preacher. Jesus is speaking of his own hour, his cross. His Passion was a birth.

Today is First Friday. We look at the Heart of Jesus, opened by the soldier's spear. From it came blood and water, and from it the Church was born. That is why our joy is a joy that no one can take away: it was born from his love, and his love does not die.

So if you are afraid today, hear the Lord's word to Paul: do not be afraid; I am with you. Come to his Heart in confession and in Communion. And from today, with Mary, let us begin to pray for the Holy Spirit, who will give us courage to speak. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, even St Paul was sometimes afraid! But Jesus told him: do not be afraid, I am with you. Jesus says the same to you when you are scared.
Today is First Friday, a day to remember Jesus' Heart, full of love. Put your hand on your heart and say: Jesus, I love you too!

intro: Theme: “No one will take your joy from you.”
The Lord's word to a fearful apostle, a judge who opened a door without knowing it, and the labour of the cross that gives birth to joy.

points.h: Do not be afraid, but speak
sub: Many in this city are my people.
q: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.

One night the Lord said to Paul in a vision, “Do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent; for I am with you, and no one will lay a hand on you to harm you, for there are many in this city who are my people.”
points.apply: Speak one word of faith this week that you have been holding back out of fear.

sub: A judge who would not judge.
q: do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the message might be fully proclaimed and all the Gentiles might hear it.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one time he protected you through people who did not even know they were helping.

sub: The pierced Heart and the birth of the Church.
A joy that cannot be taken.
q: Shall I open the womb and not deliver? says the Lord; shall I, the one who delivers, shut the womb? says your God.
When a woman is in labor, she has pain, because her hour has come. But when her child is born, she no longer remembers the anguish because of the joy of having brought a human being into the world.
points.apply: Consecrate your family to the Sacred Heart this First Friday and pray the novena to the Holy Spirit each day until Pentecost.

concl: The Lord does not always remove danger, but he removes fear by his presence: I am with you.
The cross was a labour of love; from the pierced Heart of Jesus the Church was born, and with her a joy that no one can take away.
2027-05-07.resolve: Begin the novena to the Holy Spirit today, and pray it with Mary every day until Pentecost.
